reasons-from-purpose.evidence: A unit landing page exists mainly so a teacher can get into a lesson. This is the block most visits are *for*

ranks-rather-than-lists.evidence: No full-bleed image, no stacked sub-copy — a big hero would out-rank the lesson list it's supposed to introduce.

routes-values-to-the-system.evidence: it gets the biggest column (2fr of a 2fr/1fr grid on wide screens)

respects-its-own-boundary.evidence: rendered as a horizontally scrolling strip of small cards on a muted background

would-a-designer-act-on-this.evidence: Removing any one signal should still leave the ranking legible from the others.

reasons-from-purpose.evidence: what is this screen for, and what must the reader do next — resolves to: **confirm this is the right unit, then get into a lesson.**

ranks-rather-than-lists.evidence: Two full-weight CTAs would have put two elements in competition for primacy in the same view; only one gets the primary button treatment.

routes-values-to-the-system.evidence: given the system's neutral grey card shadow (`oak-card--grey-shadow`) instead of the accent shadow the lesson cards use

respects-its-own-boundary.evidence: The design-system-usage skill explicitly allows minting a new page type when the shipped one doesn't fit

would-a-designer-act-on-this.evidence: a smaller heading *class* (`oak-heading-5` vs the list's `oak-heading-3`) and positioned *after* the lesson list rather than before it

why: Both open from what the page is for and both establish a genuine rank rather than a list, so on the two heavily-weighted criteria they are level — A's numbered primary/secondary/tertiary tiers and its 'removing any one signal should still leave the ranking legible' redundancy test are as good as anything in B. The separation is criterion 3: A carries its whole hierarchy in self-invented values ('2fr of a 2fr/1fr grid', 'a muted background', 'a small uppercase label') that route nowhere, while every value B reaches for is a real, checkable design-system class or token (oak-heading-3, oak-card-link, oak-card--grey-shadow, oak-card--flat, --bg-subtle) — I verified these exist in components.css and colors_and_type.css, and B's account of the shipped [data-page='unit'] facets/results map is accurate. B also routes its one out-of-lane decision explicitly to design-system-usage, where A simply makes layout calls in place; the margin is real but narrower than the score sheet alone suggests.
